Subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool expansion & TPS guardrail annex for Sparrow AI

Hi Elena / Rajiv —

Congrats on the usage growth — really glad Sparrow's inference footprint is scaling into new product workflows. As we discussed in last week's call, your renewal window (term ends 2026-09-30) is a good place to lock in the expanded dedicated pool and explicit tokens-per-second (TPS) guardrails to avoid throttling during peak inference windows.

Attached is a first-pass addendum that:
- Adds 8 x A100 equivalent GPUs to your reserved pool (for a total of 24 GPUs)
- Defines a base TPS guarantee of 2,000 tokens/sec sustained and a burst envelope up to 4,500 tokens/sec for 60s per minute, subject to quota and routing policies
- Describes automatic fallbacks to compatible smaller model variants with a 95% success rate SLO and automatic crediting for missed TPS during an incident window

Questions for you:
1) Procurement: can you confirm whether Sparrow requires any bespoke invoicing or a PO reference (we've included the draft term sheet in the second attachment)?
2) Tech: do the burst windows/lengths above align with the telemetry you saw on the last payer spike on 2026-07-31?
3) Legal/ops: any data residency constraints we should encode in the annex?

If that looks reasonable I can route the revised addendum through Legal and get a DocuSign link; Marcus can follow up with SLO wording clarifications.

Best,
Aisha

Elena — thanks for the quick review and great questions. Technical responses below and a short proposed tweak to the addendum language.

Key points:
1) Rolling burst: we can support a rolling-burst definition instead of a single contiguous burst window. Proposed language: 
   "Burst policy: up to 4,800 TPS for a maximum of 90 seconds per 10-minute rolling window, provided aggregate sustained usage does not exceed 2,000 TPS over a 1-hour sliding window. Excess usage beyond burst limits will be subject to throttling based on routing policies and may trigger credits as defined in Section 4.2."

2) Credits & SLO window: proposed credit trigger: 
   "If Redwood fails to meet the sustained TPS guarantee (2,000 TPS) for a contiguous 10-minute interval due to capacity misallocation or platform failure, Sparrow will receive a pro-rated credit applied to the next invoice equal to 3x the pro-rated usage cost for the impacted interval. Disputes must be raised within 30 days of the event."

3) Fallback behavior: to limit user impact we will route to a compatible model variant with a graceful degradation window of up to 5 tokens-response quality steps (example: p50 latency increase and top-k reduced); customer must opt-in to automatic fallback.

4) Routing & isolation: dedicated pool will be isolated per account with capacity headroom reserved for critical endpoints (we propose a 10% system buffer to reduce noisy-neighbor risk).

I've attached a quick rev (redwood-tps-addendum-rev1.pdf) with these edits tracked. Connor — pinging you for procurement/order flow and to confirm how PO SP-2026-338 will be referenced in our invoicing. Neha — can you confirm the legal phrasing on the credit multiplier (3x) and the dispute window?

Thanks,
Marcus
Product Solutions, Redwood Inference
(marcus_lin@redwood.com)
